page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.large is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, configured with 2 shared vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the ecs.e4.large sits in the lower performance tiers. Both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests place the instance in the bottom 10% of benchmarked servers. Memory bandwidth performance is similarly constrained, with large-block read and write speeds falling into the bottom 10%, while small-block cached reads are slightly higher but remain in the bottom 25%. Computational tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression register in the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput also rank in the bottom 10%.

Given the shared CPU allocation and lower benchmark scores, the ecs.e4.large presents a tradeoff between high memory capacity and processing throughput. The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, high-performance CPU execution. This server is best suited for lightweight database caching, development environments, basic web serving, or background tasks that benefit from a larger memory footprint but can tolerate shared CPU resources and low baseline network throughput.
